properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-08-26, continuing the hub thread.

📌 DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-a-hub-owns-designs-it-does-not-absorb-...`, which asks what RELATION should express a hub. This asks about CUSTODY AND CURRENCY: where a sub-project's design physically lives, what keeps a hub-held copy from going stale, and whether a sub-project needs a design at all. That node could be answered and leave every question here open.

═══ THE IDEA, IN HIS WORDS ═══

*"each project repo in the master repo gets a `reflow2.json` file within the hub/project-brain repo. it is almost like running adopt skill on each repo, but keeping the resulting reflow2.json within the hub/project-brain repo."*

**And he names the problem in the same breath:** *"if one of the existing repos change, then the reflow2.json in the hub repo may not track that or be current with it. I think it may be unavoidable that adopt skill must be run on each sub-project repo in a master-project to keep currency??"*

═══ ⭐ THE ANSWER MAY ALREADY BE HALF-BUILT, AND IT IS WORTH CHECKING BEFORE DESIGNING ═══

A copy going stale is not a new problem — it is one reflow2 already solves twice, and neither mechanism has been pointed here:

- `sync_status` / `req:stale-seat-knows` — a seat whose graph never caught up must not replace a shared design with a complete-but-older document. **A hub holding N copies is N seats, all of which can go stale.** The refusal machinery exists.
- **A checksum makes staleness computable rather than assumed.** A hub-held copy could carry the child export's `content_hash` and say plainly *"this copy is behind"* — which is the existing hub node's item 4 (last-export-date) with a sharper answer.

⇒ **The honest first move is measurement, not vocabulary:** does a hub-held copy plus a content hash already answer this, making the gap a REPORT rather than a mechanism?

═══ 🛑 "MUST ADOPT BE RE-RUN PER SUB-REPO?" — IT TURNS ON WHAT THE COPY IS FOR ═══

- **If the copy is a CACHE of the child's own design**, re-running `adopt` is the wrong repair: the child should EXPORT and the hub should FETCH. Re-adopting re-derives from source what the child already knows — and worse, **two adopts of the same repo need not agree.** `adopt` is a guided process with human judgement in it, so the hub's copy would drift from the child's by INTERPRETATION, not merely by age. That is a nastier drift than staleness because nothing dates it.
- **If the copy is the ONLY design and the child has none**, re-running adopt is the only route, and the currency problem is real and unavoidable.

**Nothing in the question says which**, and it decides everything downstream.

═══ HIS FINAL QUESTION, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST ═══

*"can the sub-projects exist without a reflow2.json object (either within them or contained in the master hub)?"*

⭐ **This decides whether the hub is a reflow2 feature or a different product.**

- **(i) Every sub-project has its own design; the hub links or caches.** Smallest; uses `link-projects` / `mirror_surface`. ⚠️ Counter: O-02 measured zero of seven siblings exporting — blocked on a nudge problem before a vocabulary one.
- **(ii) Sub-projects have none; the hub holds one per repo.** The idea as stated. ⚠️ Counter: the currency problem above, plus interpretation drift from repeated `adopt`.
- **(iii) Sub-projects need nothing at all; the hub indexes repos directly.** Closest to the retrieval use cases. ⚠️ Counter: **reflow2 has never read a repository's source to build a graph, and `adopt` is a guided human/agent process, not a builder.** This is a new product surface, not an extension of an existing one.

═══ ⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHT ═══

**A hub holding N copies is a second source of truth, N times over.** `changelog_view`'s reasoning — nothing is stored, because a stored changelog could disagree with the graph — applies here with MORE force, not less. Every option except (i) manufactures records that can disagree with what they describe, and catching exactly that is reflow2's whole value.

📌 **ONE MEASURED FACT BEARS ON IT:** `fact:the-hub-hand-rolled-its-own-graph-tooling-per-repo-rather-than-waiting` records a real hub carrying `codegraphs/` with a subdirectory **per repository** — option (ii)/(iii)'s shape, already built by hand. But it PREDATES reflow2, so it is inheritance rather than a verdict on what reflow2 should do. That node was corrected twice by its owner; read it before citing it.
properties.name: OPEN — if the hub holds a reflow2.json per sub-repo, what keeps each one current, and can a sub-project exist with no design of its own at all?
properties.rationale:
Recorded as its own question because it asks about CUSTODY AND CURRENCY — where a sub-project's design lives and what keeps a copy honest — which is separate from what RELATION expresses a hub, and separate again from what may CROSS a design boundary.

The three readings of "can a sub-project have no design at all" are kept apart deliberately, because they are not degrees of one answer: (i) is existing machinery, (ii) is a caching problem, and (iii) would require reflow2 to read source to build a graph — something it has never done. Collapsing them would hide that the third is a different product rather than a larger version of the first.

The strongest objection is written at full strength: every option except the first manufactures a second source of truth about a system, which is the failure reflow2 exists to detect. And the interpretation-drift point is recorded because it is the non-obvious half — two runs of a guided process on the same repo need not agree, and no date reveals that.
